messages:
Priya: Quick sync — we need to shift the panel for the Senior Infra candidate on Fri to fit an EMEA timezone (GMT+1). Can @Elena or @Samir pick up backend? Also quick rubric question: what weight are we giving to take-home vs live? link: https://redwood/internal/hiring/rubrics
Elena: I can cover backend. Prefer a 10:30–11:30 UTC window. That avoids the late afternoon for EMEA.
Samir: I can be backup — free roughly 09:00–12:00 UTC that day. Keep me on the thread if we need swaps.
Maya: Heads-up — please use rubric v2 (https://redwood/internal/hiring/rubric-v2). Default take-home weight is 30% unless the interview lead requests higher.
Priya: Thanks — @Elena please confirm the 10:30 UTC slot so I can send invites. For debrief, add a 1–2 line summary to the candidate debrief doc after the interview. I'll create a placeholder.
Elena: Confirmed for 10:30 UTC. Quick rubric clarification: how do we split system-design vs API depth? The doc is a bit terse.
Maya: Good point — let's make it explicit: system design 15 points, API/edge cases 10 points, communication 5 points. I'll update the rubric doc now.
Elena: Nice. Debrief template I'll paste into the doc so it's quick for reviewers:
```
Score (0-30): 23
Strengths: strong infra fundamentals, good debugging examples
Concerns: limited experience with service meshes
Recommendation: hire / no-hire / strong-hire (pick one)
```
Samir: That template looks good. One ask: can we add a quick checkbox for "take-home reviewed" so we know if the take-home influenced score?
Maya: Yep adding a "Take-home reviewed" checkbox and a short note field.
PeopleOps Bot: Calendar invite sent to panel (10:30 UTC). Debrief doc created: https://redwood/internal/hiring/debriefs/6768450000-infra-sr
Priya: Perfect — once the interview finishes, please paste the 1–2 bullet summary in the doc and mark the checkbox. :thumbsup:
